title: Taxonomic Biomarker Discovery with LEfSe
author: Curtis Huttenhower
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d9699d

steps.title: Standardize sample class names
steps.instruction: Convert the sample names in output/merged_abundance_table.txt to consistent class names either by manually editing the file or by applying an appropriate sed command; this prepares the file for LEfSe processing.

substeps.instruction: Open output/merged_abundance_table.txt and edit class names so they are uniform across samples.
Alternatively, run a sed command that replaces the original class identifiers with the desired consistent names.

steps.title: Format LEfSe input table
steps.instruction: Run format_input.py to create a LEfSe‑compatible table, ensuring the class information is in the first row and scaling all abundance values to the range [0, 1,000,000] (‑c 1 ‑o 1000000). Command: $ format_input.py tmp/merged_abundance_table.4lefse.txt tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse -c 1 -o 1000000

steps.title: Run LEfSe biomarker analysis
steps.instruction: Execute run_lefse.py on the formatted table and set the LDA effect‑size threshold to 4 (instead of the default 2) with the option ‑l 4. Command: $ run_lefse.py tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse.out -l 4. Note: for a more compact final image the threshold was later increased to 4.7.

steps.title: Plot biomarker effect sizes
steps.instruction: Generate a PNG image of the biomarkers and their effect sizes using plot_res.py with a resolution of 300 dpi. Command: $ plot_res.py --dpi 300 tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse.out output_images/lefse_biomarkers.png

steps.title: Generate taxonomic cladogram
steps.instruction: Create a cladogram that maps biomarkers onto the taxonomic tree with plot_cladogram.py, using 300 dpi and PNG format. Command: $ plot_cladogram.py --dpi 300 --format png tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse.out output_images/lefse_biomarkers_cladogram.png

steps.title: Plot single feature barplot
steps.instruction: Visualize the abundance distribution of an individual feature (e.g., Firmicutes) as a barplot with plot_features.py. Example command: $ plot_features.py -f one --feature_name

steps.title: Export features to zip archive
steps.instruction: Export biomarker features (or all features) into a compressed zip file using plot_features.py. To export only LEfSe‑identified biomarkers use -f diff; to export all features use -f all. Example command for biomarkers: $ plot_features.py -f diff --archive zip tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse tmp/merged_abundance_table.lefse.out biomarkers.zip
